summary: Action Park, a water and adventure park in Vernon, New Jersey run by former penny-stock promoter Gene Mulvihill from 1978 to 1996, caused thousands of injuries and several deaths through untested rides, teen staff and evaded regulation.

evidence.note: Mulvihill's background: university in 1956, Marines, then Wall Street career
penny-stock pump-and-dump schemes; Mayflower Securities suspended by the SEC in 1973
ski resorts bought; summer park conceived in 1976 and becomes Action Park in 1978
fourteen-year-olds operating rides in breach of state labor law; teen supervisors
teen employees paid to test-ride the Cannonball Loop after dummies lost limbs
self-made offshore insurance company in the Caymans, also used for money laundering
federal investigation and guilty plea to fraud, theft and conspiracy
bankruptcy and closure in the mid-1990s; later Mountain Creek and revival up to 2018

notes: Action Park is named as the bastard, so it is primary and Mulvihill secondary despite his large segment (hence no roles). Many years in the transcript are garbled; 1996 closure and 1956 graduation filled from the narrative and known facts. child-abuse covers teens given alcohol, hazed and used as ride testers; drugs only mentioned in passing.
